0.0.n: Introduces the first point or example.

0.2.n: The name of a prefecture in Japan.

0.3.n: Marks the location where the hot spring exists.

0.4.n: Makes Ehime the topic, following the location marker に.

0.5.n: A country name used here as the area of comparison.

0.6.n: Marks the area within which the hot spring ranks as oldest.

0.7.n: Placed before 古い to make it mean oldest.

0.8.n: Describes the hot spring; 一番 makes this a claim that it is the oldest.

0.9.n: Marks 日本で一番古い as the content of what people say.

0.10.n: Passive 言われる plus ている presents a commonly repeated claim, modifying the following noun.

0.11.n: The preceding description tells us what kind of hot spring is being introduced.

0.12.n: Marks 温泉 as the thing that exists.

0.13.n: The polite form of ある, used for the existence of things rather than people or animals.

1.0.n: The first digit of ３０００, which together reads as three thousand.

1.1.n: This digit is part of ３０００, not a separate spoken word.

1.2.n: This digit is part of ３０００, not a separate spoken word.

1.3.n: This token contains the final digit of ３０００ and 年, which counts years.

1.4.n: After a length of time, 前 places it that far back from now.

1.5.n: Marks three thousand years ago as the starting point of the spring's existence.

1.6.n: The plain form is used inside the claim marked by と, even though the sentence ends politely.

1.7.n: Marks the preceding statement as what people say.

1.8.n: Passive 言われる plus ています politely presents a commonly repeated claim.

2.0.n: A place name forming the first part of the hot spring's name.

2.1.n: Forms part of the proper name 道後温泉, known in English as Dogo Onsen.

2.2.n: Marks 道後温泉 as the name used with 言います.

2.3.n: The polite form of 言う; with a name followed by と, it tells us what something is called.

0.lit: First, in Ehime, there is a hot spring said to be the oldest in Japan.
0.tip: The entire phrase 日本で一番古いと言われている comes before 温泉 and describes it.

1.lit: It is said that it exists since three thousand years ago.
1.tip: A time expression followed by から gives the starting point: ３０００年前から means since three thousand years ago.

2.lit: It is called Dogo Hot Spring.
2.tip: A name followed by と言います is a common way to say what something is called.
